stem.en: In Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), the species oxidised is:

explanation.en: Zn loses two electrons to become Zn²⁺: it is oxidised (and acts as the reducing agent).

stem.en: In Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag, the oxidising agent is:

explanation.en: Ag⁺ gains electrons from Cu and is reduced to Ag, so Ag⁺ is the oxidising agent.

stem.en: According to the classical idea, which of these is oxidation?

explanation.en: Classically, oxidation is the addition of oxygen or an electronegative element, or the removal of hydrogen or an electropositive element.

stem.en: A copper rod is placed in ZnSO₄ solution and a silver rod in CuSO₄ solution. What happens?

options.en: Copper is deposited on the silver rod
Zinc is deposited on the copper rod
No reaction takes place in either beaker

explanation.en: The tendency to release electrons is Zn > Cu > Ag. Cu cannot reduce Zn²⁺, and Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺, so neither reacts.

solution.en: The tendency to release electrons is Zn > Cu > Ag.
Cu cannot reduce Zn²⁺, and Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺, so neither reacts.

stem.en: In 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O, which statement is correct?

options.en: H₂S is oxidised and SO₂ is reduced

explanation.en: S in H₂S goes −2 → 0 (oxidised) and S in SO₂ goes +4 → 0 (reduced). So H₂S is the reducing agent and SO₂ the oxidising agent.

stem.en: The oxidation number of Mn in KMnO₄ is:
The oxidation number of hydrogen in NaH is:

explanation.en: In metal hydrides, hydrogen is bonded to a less electronegative metal and has oxidation number −1.

stem.en: The oxidation number of oxygen in OF₂ is:

explanation.en: F is always −1, so x + 2(−1) = 0 ⇒ x = +2.

stem.en: The average oxidation number of iron in Fe₃O₄ is:

explanation.en: 3x + 4(−2) = 0 ⇒ x = +8/3 (one Fe²⁺ and two Fe³⁺).

stem.en: Peroxomonosulphuric acid H₂SO₅ has one peroxide (O–O) linkage. The oxidation number of S in it is:

explanation.en: Two O are peroxide (−1 each), three are −2: 2(+1) + x + 3(−2) + 2(−1) = 0 ⇒ x = +6. The naive answer +8 is impossible because S has only 6 valence electrons.

stem.en: Which reaction is a disproportionation reaction?

explanation.en: In H₂O₂, O is −1; it goes to −2 (in H₂O) and 0 (in O₂) at the same time.

stem.en: Which of these decompositions is NOT a redox reaction?

explanation.en: No element changes its oxidation number in CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.

stem.en: Which reaction does NOT take place?

explanation.en: Oxidising power is F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂, so I₂ cannot oxidise Cl⁻ to Cl₂.

stem.en: Which halogen does NOT show disproportionation?

explanation.en: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and shows only −1 in its compounds, so it cannot be oxidised and reduced at once.

solution.en: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and shows only −1 in its compounds, so it cannot be oxidised and reduced at once.

stem.en: In P₄ + 3OH⁻ + 3H₂O → PH₃ + 3H₂PO₂⁻, the oxidation number of phosphorus changes from:

explanation.en: P₄: 0. PH₃: −3 (reduced). H₂PO₂⁻: 2(+1) + x + 2(−2) = −1 ⇒ x = +1 (oxidised).

stem.en: How many moles of Fe²⁺ are oxidised by one mole of MnO₄⁻ in acidic medium?

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (Mn +7 → +2) and each Fe²⁺ gives 1 electron, so 5 Fe²⁺.

stem.en: The number of electrons gained when one Cr₂O₇²⁻ ion is reduced to Cr³⁺ is:

explanation.en: Each Cr goes +6 → +3 (3e⁻); two Cr atoms gain 6 electrons.

stem.en: In the balanced equation for acidified KMnO₄ oxidising oxalate, aMnO₄⁻ + bC₂O₄²⁻ + cH⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O, the value of c is:

explanation.en: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O; check charge: −2 − 10 + 16 = +4 = 2(+2).

stem.en: In acidic medium, the change in oxidation number of S when SO₂ is oxidised to SO₄²⁻ by Cr₂O₇²⁻, and the number of SO₂ molecules per Cr₂O₇²⁻, are:

explanation.en: S: +4 → +6 (2e⁻ each). Cr₂O₇²⁻ takes 6e⁻, so 3 SO₂ per Cr₂O₇²⁻.

solution.en: Cr₂O₇²⁻ takes 6e⁻, so 3 SO₂ per Cr₂O₇²⁻.

stem.en: In basic medium MnO₄⁻ oxidises I⁻ to IO₃⁻ and is reduced to MnO₂. The number of MnO₄⁻ ions that react with one I⁻ is:

explanation.en: I: −1 → +5 (6e⁻); Mn: +7 → +4 (3e⁻). So 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻.

stem.en: In the Daniell cell, the anode is:

explanation.en: Zinc is oxidised (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻), and oxidation occurs at the anode.

stem.en: The function of the salt bridge is to:

options.en: complete the circuit and keep the solutions electrically neutral

explanation.en: Ions move through the salt bridge, completing the internal circuit and balancing the charge in each half-cell.

stem.en: The standard electrode potential of the standard hydrogen electrode is taken as:

explanation.en: The SHE is the reference electrode and is assigned 0.00 V at all temperatures.

stem.en: Given E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = −0.44 V, E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V. A CuSO₄ solution can be stored safely in a vessel made of:

explanation.en: Only a metal with E° higher than Cu²⁺/Cu cannot reduce Cu²⁺. Silver (+0.80 V) does not react; Zn, Fe and Al would displace copper.

solution.en: Only a metal with E° higher than Cu²⁺/Cu cannot reduce Cu²⁺.
Silver (+0.80 V) does not react; Zn, Fe and Al would displace copper.

stem.en: Which is the strongest reducing agent? E°: Li⁺/Li −3.05 V, Na⁺/Na −2.71 V, Mg²⁺/Mg −2.36 V, Zn²⁺/Zn −0.76 V.

explanation.en: The most negative reduction potential means the greatest tendency to lose electrons: Li.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The oxidation number of sulphur in H₂SO₅ (peroxomonosulphuric acid) is +8.
Reason (R): Sulphur, a group 16 element, cannot show an oxidation number higher than +6.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: H₂SO₅ contains a peroxide (O–O) link, so two O atoms are −1 and three are −2: 2(+1) + x + 3(−2) + 2(−1) = 0 gives x = +6. R is true: +6 is sulphur's maximum (six valence electrons).

passage.en: Roadside breath analysers once used acidified potassium dichromate. When a driver who has been drinking blows into the tube, ethanol vapour reduces the orange dichromate ion, Cr₂O₇²⁻, and the crystals turn green because Cr³⁺ ions form. The length of the green band shows how much alcohol was present.

stem.en: What happens to the oxidation number of chromium, and what is the role of the dichromate ion?

explanation.en: In Cr₂O₇²⁻: 2x + 7(−2) = −2 → x = +6. It falls to +3 in Cr³⁺, so dichromate is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent; ethanol is oxidised.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In a Daniell cell, electrons flow through the external wire from the zinc electrode to the copper electrode.
Reason (R): Zinc has a more negative standard electrode potential than copper, so it is oxidised more readily.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both true; R explains A. E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, so Zn is oxidised (anode) and releases electrons that travel to the Cu cathode.

passage.en: A student performs three experiments. A zinc strip dipped in blue copper sulphate solution becomes coated with a reddish deposit and the blue colour fades. A copper strip dipped in zinc sulphate solution shows no change. A copper wire placed in colourless silver nitrate solution becomes coated with grey crystals and the solution slowly turns blue.

stem.en: Which is the correct order of the metals by their tendency to lose electrons (reducing power)?

explanation.en: Zn displaces Cu²⁺ (Zn is the stronger reducing agent than Cu); Cu does not displace Zn²⁺ (confirms it); Cu displaces Ag⁺ (Cu stronger than Ag). Order: Zn > Cu > Ag.

stem.en: Which of the following are disproportionation reactions? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: In H₂O₂, O goes from −1 to −2 and 0. In Cl₂, Cl goes from 0 to +1 and −1. In HNO₂, N goes from +3 to +5 (HNO₃) and +2 (NO). KClO₃ decomposition oxidises O and reduces Cl: two different elements, so it is not disproportionation.

stem.en: In which of the following does the named element have an oxidation number of +6? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: K₂Cr₂O₇: 2 + 2x − 14 = 0, x = +6. H₂SO₄: 2 + x − 8 = 0, x = +6. KMnO₄: 1 + x − 8 = 0, x = +7. CrO₅ has one oxide O (−2) and two peroxide groups (four O at −1): x − 2 − 4 = 0, x = +6.

stem.en: When MnO₄⁻ + C₂O₄²⁻ + H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of H⁺? Give an integer.

explanation.en: Mn: +7 → +2 (gains 5e⁻); C₂O₄²⁻ → 2CO₂ (loses 2e⁻). LCM 10: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂. Balance O with 8H₂O on the right and H with 16H⁺ on the left. Charge: −2 − 10 + 16 = +4 = 2(+2). Coefficient of H⁺ = 16.

stem.en: For the cell Zn | Zn²⁺ || Ag⁺ | Ag, E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V. What is ΔG° in kJ for the reaction Zn + 2Ag⁺ → Zn²⁺ + 2Ag? Give the nearest whole number (F = 96 485 C mol⁻¹).
In the reaction Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), the reducing agent is:

explanation.en: Zn loses electrons (is oxidised) and so reduces Cu²⁺; the substance that is oxidised is the reducing agent.

solution.en: Zn loses electrons (is oxidised) and so reduces Cu²⁺; the substance that is oxidised is the reducing agent.

stem.en: The average oxidation number of iron in Fe₃O₄ is:

explanation.en: 3x + 4(−2) = 0, so x = +8/3. Fe₃O₄ actually contains one Fe²⁺ and two Fe³⁺: (2 + 3 + 3)/3 = 8/3.

stem.en: Using standard reduction potentials, which metal is the strongest reducing agent?

explanation.en: The more negative the reduction potential, the greater the tendency of the metal to lose electrons, so Li is the strongest reducing agent.

solution.en: The more negative the reduction potential, the greater the tendency of the metal to lose electrons, so Li is the strongest reducing agent.

stem.en: The oxidation number of chromium in $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is:

explanation.en: $2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow 2x = 12 \Rightarrow x = +6$. +12 is the total for both Cr atoms, not the value per atom; +3 is Cr in the reduced product $\text{Cr}^{3+}$.

stem.en: The oxidation number of sulphur in peroxodisulphuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, is:

explanation.en: $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$ has one $-\text{O}-\text{O}-$ bridge: 6 O atoms are $-2$ and 2 are $-1$. So $2(+1) + 2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$. Treating all eight O as $-2$ gives the impossible +7 (sulphur cannot exceed +6, its group valence).

stem.en: The average oxidation number of sulphur in sodium tetrathionate, $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6$, is:

explanation.en: $2(+1) + 4x + 6(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow 4x = 10 \Rightarrow x = +2.5$. In the structure $^-\text{O}_3\text{S}-\text{S}-\text{S}-\text{SO}_3^-$ the two terminal S are +5 and the two bridging S are 0, which average to +2.5. +5 is only the terminal S; +2 is S in thiosulphate.

stem.en: Which of the following is a disproportionation reaction?

explanation.en: In disproportionation the same element in one oxidation state is both oxidised and reduced. In $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, O ($-1$) goes to $-2$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and to 0 in $\text{O}_2$. In $\text{KClO}_3$ decomposition, Cl is reduced but a different element (O) is oxidised. $\text{CaCO}_3$ decomposition is not redox at all, and Zn + $\text{CuSO}_4$ is a displacement reaction.

stem.en: How many moles of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ are oxidised to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ by one mole of $\text{MnO}_4^-$ in acidic solution?

explanation.en: $\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (Mn: +7 → +2). Each $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ gives one electron, so 1 mol $\text{MnO}_4^-$ oxidises 5 mol $\text{Fe}^{2+}$: $\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} + 8\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

stem.en: How many moles of $\text{KMnO}_4$ are needed to completely oxidise 1 mol of ferrous oxalate, $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$, in acidic medium?

explanation.en: $\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}$ releases 1 e; $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2$ (C: +3 → +4, two C) releases 2 e. Total 3 mol electrons per mol $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$. $\text{MnO}_4^-$ accepts 5 e. Moles of $\text{KMnO}_4 = 3/5 = 0.6$. Students who count only the oxalate get 0.4; only the iron, 0.2.

stem.en: When the equation $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + \text{I}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Cr}^{3+} + \text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$ is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, what is the coefficient of $\text{H}^+$?

explanation.en: Two Cr go from +6 to +3: 6 e gained. Six $\text{I}^-$ lose 6 e to give $3\text{I}_2$. Balance O with $7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and H with $14\text{H}^+$: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 6\text{I}^- + 14\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{I}_2 + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Charge check: $-2 - 6 + 14 = +6 = 2(+3)$.

stem.en: In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, permanganate ion oxidises iodide ion to:

explanation.en: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + \text{IO}_3^- + 2\text{OH}^-$. Mn goes +7 → +4 (3 e each, 6 e total) and I goes $-1$ → +5 (6 e). $\text{I}_2$ is the product in acidic medium; $\text{IO}_4^-$ (I = +7) is not formed.

stem.en: Which of the following can act both as an oxidising agent and as a reducing agent?

explanation.en: S in $\text{SO}_2$ is +4, between its minimum ($-2$) and maximum (+6), so it can be oxidised (to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) or reduced (to S). In $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (S +6), $\text{HNO}_3$ (N +5) and $\text{KMnO}_4$ (Mn +7) the central atom is in its highest state and can only be reduced.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Sulphuric acid cannot act as a reducing agent.
Reason (R): Sulphur in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is in its highest possible oxidation state, +6.

explanation.en: To act as a reductant the S atom would have to be oxidised further, which is impossible beyond +6 (its group valence). So A is true and R is exactly the reason. Note that H₂SO₄ can still act as an oxidising agent (e.g. hot concentrated acid with Cu).

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: In $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$, oxygen has an oxidation number of +1.
Statement II: Fluorine, the most electronegative element, has an oxidation number of $-1$ in all its compounds.

explanation.en: F is always $-1$ in compounds, so in $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$: $2x + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +1$. In $\text{OF}_2$ oxygen is +2. These are the exceptions to oxygen's usual $-2$ (others: peroxides $-1$, superoxides $-1/2$).

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Given $E^\circ$: $\text{Mg}^{2+}/\text{Mg} = -2.37$ V, $\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn} = -0.76$ V, $\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu} = +0.34$ V, $\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag} = +0.80$ V. The strongest reducing agent is:

explanation.en: The more negative the reduction potential, the greater the tendency of the metal to lose electrons, i.e. the stronger the reducing agent. Mg ($-2.37$ V) is strongest. $\text{Ag}^+$ (most positive) is the strongest oxidising agent, and Ag metal the weakest reducing agent.

stem.en: Using $E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76$ V and $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80$ V, the standard emf of the cell $\text{Zn}\,|\,\text{Zn}^{2+}\,\|\,\text{Ag}^+\,|\,\text{Ag}$ is:

explanation.en: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = 0.80 - (-0.76) = 1.56$ V. 0.04 V comes from ignoring the sign of the zinc potential; 2.36 V from wrongly doubling the silver potential because the balanced equation has $2\text{Ag}^+$ (E° is intensive); 1.10 V is the Daniell (Zn–Cu) cell.

stem.en: Given $E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76$ V, $E^\circ(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}) = -0.44$ V, $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34$ V and $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80$ V, which reaction does NOT occur spontaneously?

explanation.en: A metal displaces the ions of a metal with a higher (more positive) reduction potential. Cu (+0.34) cannot reduce $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($-0.76$): $E^\circ = -0.76 - 0.34 = -1.10$ V < 0. The other three have positive cell emf — Zn, Fe and Cu all lie below the metal whose ion they reduce.

stem.en: In the redox titration of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$, the indicator commonly used is:

explanation.en: Dichromate is orange and $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ green, so the colour change is not sharp; diphenylamine gives an intense blue at the end point. $\text{KMnO}_4$ (not dichromate) is self-indicating. Starch is used in iodometric titrations; phenolphthalein is an acid–base indicator.

options.en: No indicator — the titrant is self-indicating

stem.en: In a Daniell cell, the salt bridge:

explanation.en: The salt bridge (e.g. KCl or $\text{KNO}_3$ in agar) lets ions migrate so that charge does not build up in either beaker, completing the circuit without letting the solutions mix. Electrons flow only through the external wire; the anode is the Zn rod.

options.en: completes the inner circuit and keeps both half-cell solutions electrically neutral
allows the two solutions to mix freely

stem.en: In the reaction $2\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{S} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, according to the classical (hydrogen-removal) concept:

explanation.en: Classically, removal of hydrogen from a substance is oxidation and addition of hydrogen is reduction. $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ loses H (oxidised; S goes $-2$ → 0) and $\text{O}_2$ gains H (reduced; O goes 0 → $-2$). The electronic and oxidation-number views agree.

options.en: $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is oxidised because hydrogen is removed from it
$\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is reduced because sulphur is formed
$\text{O}_2$ is oxidised because water is formed
The reaction is not a redox reaction

stem.en: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?

explanation.en: In $\text{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$, Ca (+2), C (+4) and O ($-2$) keep their oxidation numbers. In the others: H +1 → 0 and O $-2$ → 0 in water; H $-1$ → 0 and Na +1 → 0 in NaH; Cl +5 → $-1$ and O $-2$ → 0 in $\text{KClO}_3$.

stem.en: The equivalent mass of $\text{KMnO}_4$ (M = 158 g mol$^{-1}$) when it is reduced in acidic medium is:

explanation.en: In acid, $\text{MnO}_4^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+}$: 5 e gained, so $E = 158/5 = 31.6$. In neutral/weakly alkaline medium ($\rightarrow \text{MnO}_2$, 3 e) it is 52.7; in strongly alkaline medium ($\rightarrow \text{MnO}_4^{2-}$, 1 e) it is 158.

stem.en: What volume (in mL) of 0.020 M $\text{KMnO}_4$ is required to oxidise 25.0 mL of 0.10 M oxalic acid in acidic solution?

explanation.en: Moles of oxalic acid $= 0.025 \times 0.10 = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}$. From $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 + 6\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 10\text{CO}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$, moles $\text{MnO}_4^- = \tfrac25 \times 2.5\times10^{-3} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}$. $V = 1.0\times10^{-3}/0.020 = 0.050$ L = 50 mL. Using a 1:1 ratio gives 125 mL.

stem.en: 0.5 mol of hydrazine, $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$, loses 3 mol of electrons to form a new compound Y in which all the nitrogen atoms are in the same oxidation state. What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in Y?

explanation.en: In $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$, N is $-2$. Electrons lost per mol $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4 = 3/0.5 = 6$, i.e. 3 per N atom. New oxidation number $= -2 + 3 = +1$ (as in $\text{N}_2\text{O}$). Dividing by moles but forgetting there are two N atoms gives +4.

stem.en: The reaction $\text{Cr(OH)}_3 + \text{IO}_3^- \rightarrow \text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{I}^-$ is balanced in basic medium. The coefficients of $\text{Cr(OH)}_3$, $\text{IO}_3^-$ and $\text{OH}^-$ respectively are:

explanation.en: Cr loses 3 e, I gains 6 e, so 2 Cr(OH)₃ per $\text{IO}_3^-$. Then $2\text{Cr(OH)}_3 + \text{IO}_3^- + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow 2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{I}^- + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Checks — O: 6 + 3 + 4 = 13 = 8 + 5; H: 6 + 4 = 10 = 10; charge: $-1 - 4 = -5 = -4 - 1$.

stem.en: For the self-reduction step in copper extraction, $2\text{Cu}_2\text{O} + \text{Cu}_2\text{S} \rightarrow 6\text{Cu} + \text{SO}_2$, which statement(s) is/are correct?

explanation.en: All six Cu go from +1 to 0 (6 e gained); S goes from $-2$ to +4 (6 e lost) — so 6 mol electrons per mol $\text{SO}_2$. $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ only contains reducible Cu (O stays $-2$), so it is an oxidising agent, not a reducing agent. $\text{Cu}_2\text{S}$ is both oxidant (its Cu) and reductant (its S).

options.en: Six moles of electrons are transferred per mole of $\text{SO}_2$ formed

stem.en: In which of the following does the element named have an oxidation number of +5?

explanation.en: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$: $2x = 10$, x = +5. $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$: $4 + 2x - 14 = 0$, x = +5. $\text{CrO}_5$ has two peroxide groups (butterfly structure): $x + 4(-1) + (-2) = 0$, x = +6 (not +10). $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ (Caro's acid) has one peroxide group: $2 + x - 6 - 2 = 0$, x = +6 (not +8).

stem.en:
Match the species in Column I with the oxidation number of the element named in Column II.
Column I: (P) S in $\text{S}_8$ (Q) O in $\text{KO}_2$ (R) O in $\text{BaO}_2$ (S) Os in $\text{OsO}_4$
Column II: (i) +8 (ii) −1 (iii) 0 (iv) −1/2

explanation.en: Elements in the free state are 0 ($\text{S}_8$). $\text{KO}_2$ is a superoxide ($\text{O}_2^-$): O = $-1/2$. $\text{BaO}_2$ is a peroxide ($\text{O}_2^{2-}$): O = $-1$. In $\text{OsO}_4$, $x = +8$, one of the highest oxidation states known. Swapping the peroxide and superoxide values is the usual slip.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Hydrochloric acid is not used to acidify the solution when $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is titrated against $\text{KMnO}_4$.
Reason (R): $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidises $\text{Cl}^-$ ions to $\text{Cl}_2$, so extra permanganate is consumed.

explanation.en: $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}) = 1.51$ V exceeds $E^\circ(\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-) = 1.36$ V, so permanganate oxidises chloride, giving a falsely high titre. Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is used instead. Both statements are true and R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: White phosphorus reacts with hot aqueous NaOH: $\text{P}_4 + 3\text{OH}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{PH}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$. The ratio of P atoms oxidised to P atoms reduced is:

explanation.en: P in $\text{P}_4$ is 0. In $\text{PH}_3$, P is $-3$ (reduced; 1 atom). In $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$: $2(+1) + x + 2(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +1$ (oxidised; 3 atoms). Ratio oxidised : reduced = 3 : 1. Electron check: 3 × 1 lost = 1 × 3 gained. 1 : 3 is the reversed ratio.

stem.en: What mass (in g) of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ (M = 294 g mol$^{-1}$) is needed to oxidise 0.60 mol of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ in acidic solution?

explanation.en: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 6\text{Fe}^{2+} + 14\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 6\text{Fe}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Moles dichromate $= 0.60/6 = 0.10$; mass $= 0.10 \times 294 = 29.4$ g. Taking 3 e per dichromate (one Cr only) doubles the answer to 58.8 g.

stem.en: Given $E^\circ(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}) = +0.77$ V, $E^\circ(\text{I}_2/\text{I}^-) = +0.54$ V and $E^\circ(\text{Br}_2/\text{Br}^-) = +1.09$ V. Which statement is correct?

explanation.en: $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{I}^-$: $E^\circ = 0.77 - 0.54 = +0.23$ V (spontaneous). $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{Br}^-$: $0.77 - 1.09 = -0.32$ V (not spontaneous; instead $\text{Br}_2$ oxidises $\text{Fe}^{2+}$). $\text{I}_2$ + $\text{Fe}^{2+}$: $0.54 - 0.77 < 0$, so it does not occur.
